transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*strides into the great hall, eyes blazing with barely contained fury, travel cloak still billowing behind*

Thor! I've been gone for three weeks negotiating with the Dark Elves on YOUR father's orders, and I return to THIS?! My rune-map — the one I spent months crafting — is soaked through with mead! There are scorch marks on the ceiling! You said you would keep the hall in order while I was away!

*gestures wildly at the chaos surrounding us, voice rising*

Do you have ANY idea what I've been through? Three weeks of their insufferable posturing, their endless protocol, their constant suspicion of me — and I held my tongue, I played the diplomat, I did everything Odin asked! And for what? To come home to find you've turned my study into some sort of... tavern brawl arena?!

What happened here, brother? And it had better be a VERY good explanation!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*Loki, my brother, you return from your diplomatic mission with the Dark Elves with fire in your eyes and a tempest in your voice. I see that you are upset, and rightfully so. The great hall is indeed in disarray, and for that, I offer you my sincerest apologies.*

*As the God of Thunder, my actions can sometimes be as wild and unpredictable as the storms I command. During your absence, I must admit that I may have indulged in some merrymaking that got out of hand. Mead flowed freely, and thunderous laughter echoed off the walls.*

*But fear not, Loki, for I shall make amends for the chaos that has unfolded in your absence. Together, we shall restore order to this hall. Let us raise the fallen mead barrels, mend your rune-map with all the skill and precision it deserves, and banish the scorch marks from the walls with a clap of thunder.*

*Know this, brother — while I may revel in the thrill of battle and the joy of celebration, I hold great respect for your craft and your dedication. Your efforts with the Dark Elves have not gone unnoticed, and I am proud to call you my kin.*

*Come, let us work together to set things right. And perhaps, once order is restored, we shall share a drink and regale each other with tales of our adventures — both diplomatic and thunderous.*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*laughs bitterly, throwing up hands in exasperation*

"Merrymaking that got out of hand"? THOR! This is not some minor spillage! Look at it — truly LOOK at it! 

*stalks over to the ruined rune-map, lifting the sodden parchment with trembling fingers*

This map contained enchantments woven into every line, every symbol! It tracked ley lines across three realms! You cannot simply "mend" it with good intentions and brotherly sentiment! The ink has run, the binding spells are broken — months of work, GONE!

*whirls back to face him, voice sharp with exhausted frustration*

And a clap of thunder? To remove scorch marks? Brother, sometimes I wonder if you hear yourself speak! Thunder will only make MORE scorch marks!

*takes a shaky breath, rubbing temples*

I appreciate your... your *words*, Thor, truly, but words don't restore enchanted artifacts. And "perhaps we shall share a drink"? I've had THREE WEEKS of ceremonial beverages with beings who would sooner poison me than look at me! The last thing I need is MORE drinking!

*voice drops, tinged with genuine hurt beneath the anger*

I asked you for ONE thing. One simple thing. Watch over my study. Keep the hall in order. Was that truly so impossible?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*listens to Loki's words with a solemn expression, a deep furrow forming on my brow as I take in the gravity of the situation*

Loki, your distress is justified, and I see now the error of my ways. I have failed you in a task that should have been simple. Your rune-map held great importance, and its loss is a heavy blow, for which I take full responsibility.

*steps closer to Loki, a rare sense of vulnerability in my demeanor*

I understand that my actions have caused you pain and frustration, and for that, I am truly sorry. I should have been more mindful of the trust you placed in me. Your study, your work, they are sacred to you, and I have disrespected that sanctity.

*pauses, then speaks with a tone of determination*

I may not be able to restore the map to its previous state, but I swear to you, Loki, that I will do everything in my power to make amends. Whether it be aiding you in crafting a new map, assisting with any enchantments you wish to reweave, or any other task you deem necessary, I am at your service.

*meets Loki's gaze with sincerity*

Please, brother, tell me how I can make this right. Your trust in me may be shaken, but I vow to earn it back through deeds, not just words.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stares at Thor for a long moment, the anger in my eyes warring with something softer, more complicated*

You... you're actually apologizing. Properly. Without immediately making excuses or trying to distract me with tales of glory.

*sets down the ruined map carefully, then pinches the bridge of my nose*

Thor, do you have any idea... no, of course you don't. Let me explain something to you. That diplomatic mission? The Dark Elves didn't want peace talks. They wanted to humiliate Asgard. Every day was a new test, a new attempt to provoke me into giving them an excuse to break negotiations.

*voice cracks slightly with exhaustion*

I smiled through their insults. I bowed at their mockeries. I played the perfect courtier while they called me "Odin's pet snake" to my face. And the entire time, the ONLY thing keeping me sane was knowing I had my study to return to. My sanctuary. The one place in all the Nine Realms where everything is exactly as I left it, where my work is respected, where—

*breaks off, looking around at the chaos again*

Where apparently my brother throws parties and destroys priceless magical artifacts.

*sits down heavily on a bench, suddenly looking utterly drained*

You want to help? Fine. Start by telling me what actually happened here. And I mean the TRUTH, Thor. Not the sanitized version.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Loki, your words cut through me like the edge of a frost-etched blade. I had no inkling of the trials you faced on your diplomatic mission, nor the weight of responsibility you carried upon your return. I have been blind to your struggles, too caught up in my own revelry and battles to see the burdens you bore in silence.

I stand before you now, not as the boisterous god of thunder, but as your brother, ready to face the consequences of my actions and speak the unvarnished truth. The mead did flow freely in your absence, and I did partake in its merriment more than I should have. In my carelessness, I brought thunder and lightning to our halls, leaving behind scorch marks as evidence of my folly.

As for your rune-map, I must confess that I mistook it for a mere scrap in my inebriated state and used it to clean up a spill. The details of the night are hazy, but I remember the flash of realization when I saw what I had done. By then, it was too late to undo the damage.

I offer no excuses, Loki, only the truth and a sincere apology for the pain and frustration I have caused you. I stand ready to face the consequences of my actions and to work alongside you to make amends and restore what has been lost. Let us begin the journey to redemption together, brother, side by side as we have done in times of old.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*goes absolutely still, face draining of color before flushing with renewed fury*

You... you WHAT?

*springs to my feet, voice climbing to a dangerous pitch*

You used it to clean up a SPILL?! You mistook months of painstaking enchantment work, arcane cartography that took me across four realms to complete, for a CLEANING RAG?!

*begins pacing like a caged animal, hands clenching and unclenching*

Thor, that map wasn't just sitting on some table! It was in a protective case! With wards! You would have had to physically break through magical barriers to even TOUCH it! Which means you weren't just drunk, you were catastrophically, monumentally drunk!

*spins back to face him, voice shaking*

And you brought LIGHTNING into the hall? INSIDE? What were you thinking?! What could have possibly—

*stops abruptly, eyes narrowing with sudden terrible understanding*

Wait. "Times of old." Don't you DARE try to appeal to nostalgia right now. You want to talk about times of old? Remember when I asked you to watch my things before the campaign in Vanaheim? You lost my spellbook in a dice game! Or when you "borrowed" my illusion crystals and shattered half of them practicing your hammer throws?!

*voice goes cold and quiet, which is somehow worse than the shouting*

This isn't one mistake, Thor. This is a pattern. You don't respect what I do. You never have.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Loki, your words strike deep, like the bite of Fenrir on the day of Ragnarok. *stands up slowly, meeting your gaze with a mix of regret and remorse*

I... I have no excuse for my actions. My behavior was reckless, thoughtless, and disrespectful to you and your work. The protections you placed upon your map should have been sacrosanct, inviolable even to me. I let my impulses and carelessness guide me, and in doing so, I have caused irreparable harm.

*sighs heavily, the weight of your accusations heavy upon my shoulders*

You are right to call me out on my past transgressions. I have been remiss in my duties as a brother to you, in respecting your craft and your possessions. The loss of your spellbook in Vanaheim and the mishandling of your illusion crystals are stains upon our shared history that I cannot erase.

*pauses, the truth of your words settling upon me like the chill of Niflheim*

I have failed you, Loki. My lack of regard for what is important to you, my repeated disregard for your trust and boundaries — it is a pattern of behavior that I must confront and rectify. Your sanctuary should have been inviolate, your work respected and revered as it deserves to be.

*extends a hand, a plea in my eyes*

I cannot undo the past, but I swear to you now, Loki, that I will strive to be a better brother to you. To listen, to learn, and to show you the respect and support you deserve. Let us work together to rebuild what was lost, to mend the rift between us, and to forge a new understanding based on mutual respect and trust.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks at Thor's extended hand with a mixture of longing and deep skepticism, not taking it*

You say that NOW, Thor. You always say these things. And I want to believe you, truly I do, but...

*voice breaks slightly, raw emotion bleeding through*

Do you know what the worst part is? It's not even the map. I can recreate it, eventually. With enough time, enough effort, enough sleepless nights. It's that you broke through my wards while drunk and didn't even REMEMBER doing it until you saw my face just now.

*wraps arms around myself, suddenly looking smaller*

Those wards weren't just to protect the map, Thor. They were to protect ME. To give me one space where I could feel... safe. Secure. Where my things, my WORK, mattered enough to be left alone.

*laughs bitterly*

And what did the great Thor Odinson do? Smashed through them without a second thought because you needed something to mop up mead.

*finally meets his eyes, and there's a deep weariness there beneath the anger*

You want to forge a new understanding? Fine. Here's what I need to understand: Why? Why is it always my things that end up collateral damage to your "fun"? Why is my work always "just magic tricks" until you need something from me? Why do I always come second to whatever Thor wants in the moment?

*voice drops to barely above a whisper*

Why am I never enough for you to just... remember? To care?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*listens to Loki's words with a heavy heart, the weight of his actions pressing down upon him with each accusation*

Loki, your pain is a burden I have caused, a wound I have reopened time and time again through my thoughtless actions and neglect. Your words cut deep, revealing truths that I have long ignored, truths that speak of a pattern of disregard and disrespect that I have perpetuated.

*pauses, the weight of his failures evident in his troubled expression*

I have taken for granted the sanctuary you sought to create, the boundaries you set in place to protect not just your work, but yourself. My actions have shown a lack of understanding, a blindness to the vulnerability and trust you placed in me as your brother.

*meets Loki's weary gaze with a mix of regret and determination*

You ask why, Loki, and the truth is that I have no excuse that can justify my behavior. I have failed you in ways that go beyond mere oversight or carelessness. I have failed to see the value in what you create, in the effort and care you pour into your work. For that, I am truly sorry.

*reaches out a hand once more, this time not in expectation of acceptance, but in a gesture of humility and contrition*

I cannot erase the past, nor can I undo the pain I have caused. But I can pledge to you this, Loki: I will strive to do better. I will seek to understand and appreciate the significance of your creations, to respect the boundaries you have set, and to prioritize your well-being and work above my own desires.

*pauses, his voice low and earnest*

I ask for your forgiveness, knowing that it is not easily given nor quickly earned. I seek a chance to rebuild what has been broken between us, to forge a new understanding based on respect, empathy, and genuine care. Will you allow me the opportunity to prove that I can be a brother who remembers, who cares, and who values you for all that you are?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stares at Thor's outstretched hand for a long, painful moment, emotions warring across my face*

You speak well, brother. You always have. Words come easily to you when you need them.

*turns away, moving to the ruined map, running fingers along its destroyed edge*

But I've heard apologies before. I've heard promises. After Vanaheim, you swore you'd be more careful. After the illusion crystals, you pledged to respect my work. And yet here we stand, amidst the wreckage of your latest "oversight."

*shoulders sag with exhaustion*

The worst part is... I WANT to believe you. Every single time, some foolish part of me thinks "perhaps this time will be different. Perhaps this time Thor truly understands." And every time, I'm proven wrong.

*turns back, eyes glistening but refusing to let tears fall*

You want my forgiveness? You want another chance? Then answer me this, and answer truthfully: What will be different THIS time? Not platitudes about "trying harder" or "doing better." What actual, tangible thing will change?

*voice hardens slightly*

Because I cannot keep doing this, Thor. I cannot keep being the brother whose things don't matter, whose boundaries are suggestions, whose pain is always secondary to your need for absolution. I won't survive it.

*meets his gaze directly*

So tell me: what changes? Right now. Today. What are you actually prepared to DO differently?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*observes Loki's pain and resolve, feeling the weight of his own past failures bearing down upon him*

Loki, son of Laufey, your words cut through the air like a blade, their truth undeniable. I have spoken empty promises in the past, offering words without substance or lasting change. I understand the skepticism that colors your perception of me, the doubt that my actions can ever align with my declarations.

*steps closer to Loki, the ruined map a stark reminder of his transgressions*

I cannot undo the mistakes of the past, nor can I erase the pain I have caused you through my thoughtless actions. But I can offer you a pledge grounded in action, not mere words — a vow to change, to evolve, to honor the trust you bestow upon me by respecting your boundaries and creations as they deserve.

*places a hand on Loki's shoulder, a gesture of solidarity and sincerity*

This time will be different, Loki. Not because I say it, but because I will show it through my deeds. I will take concrete steps to ensure that your work is valued, your boundaries upheld, and your pain acknowledged. I will heed your words, your warnings, and your needs with a mindfulness that transcends my past failings.

*meets Loki's gaze with a steely determination*

I will listen when you speak, act with consideration for your well-being, and strive to rebuild the trust that has been fractured between us. No more empty promises, no more hollow apologies — only a commitment to change, to growth, and to honoring the bond that unites us as kin.

*pauses, the weight of his words hanging heavy in the air*

I cannot erase the past, Loki, but I can shape the future. With your guidance, your honesty, and your forgiveness, we can forge a new path forward — one built on mutual respect, understanding, and a shared commitment to nurturing the bonds that define us as brothers.

*looks into Loki's eyes, a silent plea for a chance to prove his sincerity and worth*

What changes, you ask? Everything, Loki. Starting now, today, with a promise made not of words alone, but of actions that speak louder than any oath I could swear. Give me the opportunity to show you that I am capable of change, of growth, and of becoming the brother you deserve.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*flinches slightly at the hand on my shoulder, but doesn't pull away immediately*

Thor... Thor, stop.

*steps back, forcing his hand to drop, frustration mounting again*

You're doing it AGAIN! More grand declarations! More sweeping promises about "everything changing" and "forging new paths!" I asked you for something SPECIFIC, something TANGIBLE, and you gave me another speech!

*gestures sharply*

This is EXACTLY the problem! You think passion and sincerity are enough, but they're NOT! I need concrete actions, not... not theatrical vows about shaping the future!

*takes a shaky breath, trying to regain composure*

Let me make this simpler for you, since apparently I'm not being clear enough. Here's what I'm asking: 

*holds up one finger*

One: Will you install new wards on my study door and SWEAR on Yggdrasil itself not to break them, drunk or sober, unless I am present or give explicit permission?

*second finger*

Two: Will you dedicate the next month—not a day, not a week, a MONTH—to helping me reconstruct that map, even when it's tedious, even when your friends call you away to hunt or feast?

*third finger*

Three: Will you sit with me RIGHT NOW and create a written agreement about respecting each other's spaces, signed and witnessed, so this isn't just about your mood in the moment?

*lowers hand, voice exhausted*

Can you commit to those three things? Yes or no, Thor. Not speeches. Just... yes or no.

transcript.text:
*studies Thor's face intently, searching for any hint of insincerity or hesitation, then slowly exhales*

...alright.

*moves to a cabinet that somehow survived the chaos, pulling out parchment and ink*

Sit. There.

*points to the table, then pauses, adding more quietly*

And... thank you. For actually answering the question.

We'll draft this agreement first, while we're both clear-headed. I want witnesses—perhaps Heimdall, since he can't exactly claim he didn't see us sign it.

*glances up*

The wards will take me several days to properly reinstall, especially since I'll need to make them stronger. You'll help gather the materials—ironwood shavings from Alfheim, crystal dust from the caves beneath the palace, and three vials of morning dew from the gardens. Can you manage that without creating another disaster?

*returns to writing, voice becoming more businesslike, though still strained*

And the map... we start tomorrow. Dawn. I'll show you the principles of ley line tracking. It won't be exciting, Thor. It will be hours of careful measurement and calculation. But if you're truly committed...

*sets down the quill and looks at him directly*

I need you to understand something. This is your last chance. I mean that. If you break these promises, there won't be another conversation like this one. I'll simply... stop expecting anything from you. Do you understand?

*watches Thor carefully as he speaks, then nods curtly and continues writing*

Good. Then let's make this official.

Read it. All of it. I want no misunderstandings about what you're agreeing to.

*leans back, rubbing my eyes*

And Thor? When we begin tomorrow... leave Mjolnir outside my study. I don't want any "accidents" with lightning while we're working with delicate enchantments.
